passages.text: Soon Nahash the Ammonite came up and laid siege to Jabesh-gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to him, “Make a treaty with us, and we will serve you.”
passages.sermon:
Nahash was an Ammonite leader.
Nahash came up against Jabesh-gilead.
Nahash laid siege to the city.
All the men of Jabesh spoke to Nahash.
They said, “Make a treaty with us.
We will serve you.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֗עַל נָחָשׁ֙ הָֽעַמּוֹנִ֔י וַיִּ֖חַן עַל־ יָבֵ֣שׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ כָּל־ אַנְשֵׁ֤י יָבֵישׁ֙ אֶל־ נָחָ֔שׁ כְּרָת־ לָ֥נוּ בְרִ֖ית וְנַעַבְדֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: But Nahash the Ammonite replied, “I will make a treaty with you on one condition, that I may put out everyone’s right eye and bring reproach upon all Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Nahash was the king of the Ammonites.
Nahash spoke to the men of Jabesh-gilead.
Nahash said, “I will make a treaty with you on one condition.
I will put out the right eye of every one of you.
I will bring shame on all Israel by doing this.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם נָחָשׁ֙ הָעַמּוֹנִ֔י בְּזֹאת֙ אֶכְרֹ֣ת לָכֶ֔ם בִּנְק֥וֹר לָכֶ֖ם כָּל־ עֵ֣ין יָמִ֑ין וְשַׂמְתִּ֥יהָ חֶרְפָּ֖ה עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: “Hold off for seven days,” replied the elders of Jabesh, “and let us send messengers throughout Israel. If there is no one to save us, we will surrender to you.”
passages.sermon:
The elders of Jabesh spoke to Nahash the Ammonite.
They said, “Wait for seven days.
Let us send messengers through all the territory of Israel.
If no one comes to save us, we will come out to you.
We will surrender to you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו זִקְנֵ֣י יָבֵ֗ישׁ הֶ֤רֶף לָ֙נוּ֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים וְנִשְׁלְחָה֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאִם־ אֵ֥ין מוֹשִׁ֛יעַ אֹתָ֖נוּ וְיָצָ֥אנוּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and relayed these words in the hearing of the people, they all wept aloud.
passages.sermon:
Messengers arrived at Gibeah, where Saul lived.
They spoke the words of the men from Jabesh to the people.
The people heard the message.
All the people raised their voices.
They wept loudly.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים֙ גִּבְעַ֣ת שָׁא֔וּל וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַיִּשְׂא֧וּ כָל־ הָעָ֛ם אֶת־ קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּֽוּ׃

passages.text: Just then Saul was returning from the field, behind his oxen. “What troubles the people?” asked Saul. “Why are they weeping?” And they relayed to him the words of the men from Jabesh.
passages.sermon:
Saul was a man from Israel.
Saul was returning from the field.
He walked behind his oxen.
Saul saw the people.
The people were weeping.
Saul asked, “What troubles the people?”
He also asked, “Why are they weeping?”
The people answered Saul.
They told Saul the words of the men from Jabesh.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֣ה שָׁא֗וּל בָּ֣א אַחֲרֵ֤י הַבָּקָר֙ מִן־ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל מַה־ לָּעָ֖ם כִּ֣י יִבְכּ֑וּ וַיְסַ֨פְּרוּ־ ל֔וֹ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֖י אַנְשֵׁ֥י יָבֵֽישׁ׃

passages.text: When Saul heard their words, the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he burned with great anger.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul heard the words of the messengers.
The Spirit of God came powerfully upon Saul.
Saul became very angry.
passages.original: וַתִּצְלַ֤ח רֽוּחַ־ אֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־ שָׁא֔וּל בְּשָׁמְעוֹ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּ֥חַר אַפּ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: He took a pair of oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent them by messengers throughout the land of Israel, proclaiming, “This is what will be done to the oxen of anyone who does not march behind Saul and Samuel.” Then the terror of the LORD fell upon the people, and they turned out as one man.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
He took a pair of oxen.
He cut the oxen into pieces.
He sent the pieces by messengers.
He sent them throughout the land of Israel.
He gave a message with the pieces.
He said, “This will happen to the oxen of anyone who does not follow Saul and Samuel.”
The LORD caused great fear to fall on the people.
All the people came out together as one.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּח֩ צֶ֨מֶד בָּקָ֜ר וַֽיְנַתְּחֵ֗הוּ וַיְשַׁלַּ֞ח בְּכָל־ גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ בְּיַ֣ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֣ים׀ לֵאמֹר֒ אֲשֶׁר֩ אֵינֶ֨נּוּ יֹצֵ֜א אַחֲרֵ֤י שָׁאוּל֙ וְאַחַ֣ר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל כֹּ֥ה יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה לִבְקָר֑וֹ וַיִּפֹּ֤ל פַּֽחַד־ יְהוָה֙ עַל־ הָעָ֔ם וַיֵּצְא֖וּ כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: And when Saul numbered them at Bezek, there were 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul gathered the people at Bezek.
He counted the men of Israel.
There were 300,000 Israelites.
He also counted the men of Judah.
There were 30,000 men of Judah.
passages.original: וַֽיִּפְקְדֵ֖ם בְּבָ֑זֶק וַיִּהְי֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אֶ֔לֶף וְאִ֥ישׁ יְהוּדָ֖ה שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃

passages.text: So they said to the messengers who had come, “Tell the men of Jabesh-gilead: ‘Deliverance will be yours tomorrow by the time the sun is hot.’ ” And when the messengers relayed this to the men of Jabesh, they rejoiced.
passages.sermon:
The leaders spoke to the messengers who arrived.
They gave the messengers a message for the men of Jabesh-gilead.
They said, “Tell the men of Jabesh-gilead this message.
Tomorrow you will have deliverance.
This will happen when the sun is hot.”
The messengers went to Jabesh.
They told the men of Jabesh the message.
The men of Jabesh rejoiced.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ לַמַּלְאָכִ֣ים הַבָּאִ֗ים כֹּ֤ה תֹֽאמְרוּן֙ לְאִישׁ֙ יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֔ד מָחָ֛ר תִּהְיֶֽה־ לָכֶ֥ם תְּשׁוּעָ֖ה בְּחֹם הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֗ים וַיַּגִּ֛ידוּ לְאַנְשֵׁ֥י יָבֵ֖ישׁ וַיִּשְׂמָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: Then the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Tomorrow we will come out, and you can do with us whatever seems good to you.”
passages.sermon: The men of Jabesh spoke to Nahash.\r\nThey said, “Tomorrow we will come out to you.”\r\nThey said, “You may do to us whatever seems good to you.”
passages.original: וַֽיֹּאמְרוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יָבֵ֔ישׁ מָחָ֖ר נֵצֵ֣א אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם לָּ֔נוּ כְּכָל־ הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: The next day Saul organized the troops into three divisions, and during the morning watch they invaded the camp of the Ammonites and slaughtered them, until the hottest part of the day. And the survivors were so scattered that no two of them were left together.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
The next day, Saul acted.
Saul organized the people into three groups.
Saul led the people.
They entered the camp of the Ammonites early in the morning.
They attacked the Ammonites.
They fought until the day became hot.
Some Ammonites survived.
The survivors ran away in every direction.
No two survivors stayed together.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַיָּ֨שֶׂם שָׁא֣וּל אֶת־ הָעָם֮ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁים֒ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ בְתוֹךְ־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ בְּאַשְׁמֹ֣רֶת הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֶת־ עַמּ֖וֹן עַד־ חֹ֣ם הַיּ֑וֹם וַיְהִ֤י הַנִּשְׁאָרִים֙ וַיָּפֻ֔צוּ וְלֹ֥א נִשְׁאֲרוּ־ בָ֖ם שְׁנַ֥יִם יָֽחַד׃

passages.text: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who said that Saul should not reign over us? Bring those men here so we can kill them!”
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to Samuel.
They asked about Saul.
They said, “Who said Saul should not be our king?”
They demanded those men be brought forward.
They said, “Bring those men here.”
They wanted to kill those men.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָעָם֙ אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל מִ֣י הָאֹמֵ֔ר שָׁא֖וּל יִמְלֹ֣ךְ עָלֵ֑ינוּ תְּנ֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וּנְמִיתֵֽם׃

passages.text: But Saul ordered, “No one shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to the people.
Saul gave a command.
He said, “No one will die today.”
He explained his reason.
He said, “Today the LORD saved Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל לֹֽא־ יוּמַ֥ת אִ֖ישׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֥י הַיּ֛וֹם עָשָֽׂה־ יְהוָ֥ה תְּשׁוּעָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet and leader in Israel.
Samuel spoke to the people of Israel.
Samuel said, “Let us go to Gilgal.”
Samuel said, “We will renew the kingship there.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־ הָעָ֔ם לְכ֖וּ וְנֵלְכָ֣ה הַגִּלְגָּ֑ל וּנְחַדֵּ֥שׁ שָׁ֖ם הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃

passages.text: So all the people went to Gilgal and confirmed Saul as king in the presence of the LORD. There they sacrificed peace offerings before the LORD, and Saul and all the Israelites rejoiced greatly.
passages.sermon:
All the people of Israel went to Gilgal.
They went together.
They made Saul king at Gilgal.
They did this before the LORD.
They offered peace offerings there.
They gave these offerings before the LORD.
Saul rejoiced there.
All the Israelites rejoiced very much.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכ֨וּ כָל־ הָעָ֜ם הַגִּלְגָּ֗ל וַיַּמְלִכוּ֩ שָׁ֨ם אֶת־ שָׁא֜וּל לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ בַּגִּלְגָּ֔ל וַיִּזְבְּחוּ־ שָׁ֛ם זְבָחִ֥ים שְׁלָמִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׂמַ֨ח שָׁ֥ם שָׁא֛וּל וְכָל־ אַנְשֵׁ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־ מְאֹֽד׃פ
